location: src/haute/_trace_correlation.py:186-189 (_build_value_match_expr); crash surfaces via _match_columns_by_row_index:255-261 and _find_matching_row:349, called unguarded from _correlate_rows_posthoc:650
title: _build_value_match_expr crashes the whole trace on dtype-asymmetric shared columns (numeric value vs string column, or NaN/inf value vs non-float column)
description: _build_value_match_expr only reconciles dtypes in ONE direction: when the match value is a str it casts the column to Utf8 (line 188), so 'string-value vs numeric-column' works. But when the value is numeric and the parent column is a string, control falls to `pl.col(column) == value` (line 189), and Polars raises ComputeError: 'cannot compare string with numeric type'. Symmetrically, when the value is a raw float NaN/inf the function emits `pl.col(column).is_nan()` / `is_infinite()` (lines 177-185), which raise InvalidOperationError if that same column is non-float (e.g. Utf8) in the parent. Because the value-matching path runs the expression inside `indexed.select(...)` (_match_columns_by_row_index, lines 255-261) and `_correlate_rows_posthoc` calls `_find_matching_row` WITHOUT any try/except (trace.py:504 and _trace_correlation.py:650), the exception propagates out of the entire post-hoc correlation, turning a 'click a price to trace' request into a hard 500 for any pipeline whose graph changes a shared column's dtype across a non-1:1 transform. This is a realistic shape: a node that casts a string code/id column to Int64 (or vice-versa) while also filtering/aggregating (so the same-row-count positional fast path at line 634 is bypassed and value matching is reached). Note the fast path itself is safe because it uses the pure-Python `_trace_values_match` (line 644), so the trigger is precisely: value-matching fallback + a shared column whose dtype differs between parent and child.
evidence: Reproduced end-to-end against the real function: parent_df = pl.DataFrame({'code':['10','20','30'],'v':[1,2,3]}); child_df = parent_df.filter(pl.col('v')>1).with_columns(pl.col('code').cast(pl.Int64)); _correlate_rows_posthoc({'p':parent_df,'c':child_df}, ['p','c'], {'c':['p']}, 'c', 0, node_map=...) raises `ComputeError: cannot compare string with numeric type (i32)` from `[(col("code")) == (dyn int: 20)]`. Direct expr check: df=pl.DataFrame({'x':['1','2','3']}); df.select(_build_value_match_expr('x',2)) -> ComputeError. And df=pl.DataFrame({'s':['a','b']}); df.select(_build_value_match_expr('s',float('nan'))) -> InvalidOperationError `is_nan` not supported for dtype `str`. The string-value-vs-numeric-column direction works because of the cast at line 188; the numeric-value-vs-string-column direction has no equivalent guard and hits line 189. No existing test covers a dtype-asymmetric shared column (grep of tests/ for the build_value_match_expr / 'cannot compare string with numeric' shows none), so loud-crash here is not an intended contract — the function is meant to either match (it casts in the mirror case) or fall through to the (None,-1) 'no match' result, not to abort the trace.
behavior_preservation: Fix should cast the column to Utf8 and compare stringwise (mirroring line 188) whenever the column dtype and the value type are incompatible — or guard with a dtype check so a non-matching dtype yields a False predicate rather than an exception — so correlation degrades to 'no match' (the function's documented fail-soft) instead of crashing the whole trace.
